title: Inbound capture and speed to lead
origin: ClimbOS synthesis (original proposal) from the member frameworks; author guidance is cited by finding id, proposed rules are labelled 'proposed'.
decision_task: How inbound forms and first replies should qualify and respond so good leads aren't lost and misfits are redirected politely.
applies_when: Inbound enquiries arrive by form, email or phone
required_inputs: Response time from enquiry to first reply
evidence_requirements: which qualifiers can be seen publicly
missing_data_behavior: No response-time data: measure for two weeks first.

decision_branches.if: Form asks what could be looked up

decision_branches.then: Hard-qualifier reply that states fit criteria and offers an alternative.

implementation_steps: One clear demo or contact call to action
Short form: name, company, work email, phone, plus non-observable qualifiers
Show a phone number; send an honest automatic reply
Respond in minutes with an answer and one next step
Use the hard-qualifier template for likely misfits
dependencies: a website with a request form or booking page

cash_and_labor_requirements.measurement: Time to first response, contact rate, meetings

guardrails: Call and touch counts stay within the sales-follow-up caps.
Dated lead-response studies are context, not targets.
Sensible hours for the lead's time zone
alternatives_when_constrained: No site traffic: outbound or warm intros generate the first inbound
stop_conditions: Response time drifting past an hour in working hours: add an automatic reply or a missed-call text-back (plays-local)
review_triggers: Owner's numbers or business type change
A dated benchmark this playbook mentions is superseded
Long forms asking what the site already shows
Chat widgets with no one answering

contextual_heuristic.rule: proposed: lead forms ask only for qualifiers that can't be found from the company domain; each extra field needs a stated reason.
proposed: likely-unqualified inbound gets a hard-qualifier email instead of a meeting offer.
proposed: the MIT/InsideSales response-time figure is shown only as a dated, directional example.
